messages:
Mia: Noticing intermittent p95 spikes on obs-ingest after last coalescer tweak. Looks like spikes line up with the coalescer window edges. Need a quick sync on SLA impact and ownership.
Ashwin: Can you share the timespan + panel? :eyes:
Mia: 2026-03-21 18:05-18:50 PT. Panel: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/ingest/coalescer?from=now-2h
Mia: Config pushed in v2.3: ```coalescer:
  window_ms: 25
  max_batch_items: 200
  max_batch_bytes: 524288
  ordering: best_effort
```
Sam: We intentionally lowered window_ms to 25 to reduce single-request latency. Tradeoff: smaller batches -> more CPU + lower throughput. At current qps, batch fill ~60%.
Ashwin: If fill is only 60% then many batches are suboptimal. Bumping to 50ms would likely raise fill to ~85% and reduce per-token cost. But that could add tail latency for single-request flows.
Jess: Can we do adaptive windowing? Increase window when queue depth high, shrink when low. Who implements the policy? ingest or platform?
Sam: Ingest runtime can implement an adaptive loop (target batch fullness). But Platform should own rollout, SLOs, and the feature flagging.
Mia: Another concern: merging semantics could obscure request/span boundaries used by billing and attribution. I ran a 10m diff: larger windows reduce envelope overhead -> ~3.4% cost savings, but ~0.18% of traces had merged boundaries that normalized differently for billing lookups.
Ashwin: Important: billing relies on a deterministic key per-request. If we merge envelopes without preserving boundary metadata, downstream lookups may map tokens to wrong tenants.
Sam: Suggestion: add minimal boundary markers to merged envelope headers (one-bit flags, or small boundary index). That keeps billing intact and is tiny metadata. We'll measure delta.
Jess: Action plan: run a 3-arm experiment. A) current 25ms baseline, B) fixed 50ms, C) adaptive (25ms -> 100ms scale based on fullness). Canary 2% traffic each. Rollout guard: rollback if p95 > baseline+10ms or boundary-missing-rate > 0.5%.
Mia: I'll prepare the PROM eval set + replay harness to validate no functional regressions and to compute cost delta.
Sam: Telemetry to collect: p50/p95/p99 ingest latency, batch_fill_ratio, cpu_percent, tokens_per_sec, boundary_marker_missing_count, billing-mismatch-count, per-tenant token delta.
Ashwin: Also validate that adding markers doesn't meaningfully increase token size. Keep them in envelope headers (binary flag) to avoid per-token blowup.
Jess: I'll create canary lanes and the rollout runbook. Will include safe rollback triggers and who pages. Platform will own the canary promotion policy.
deploy-bot: deploy v2.3 -> coalescer-window feature toggled by @Sam at 2026-03-21T18:12:03Z :rocket:
Mia: Quick question: adaptive algorithm parameters? I suggest: target_fill=85%, min_window=25ms, max_window=100ms, scale_factor=1.5. Keep rate of window changes <= 1/30s to avoid oscillation.
Sam: Sounds reasonable. Ingest will implement a leaky-integrator approach with hysteresis to avoid thrash. We'll start conservative.
Ashwin: For billing side, add a reconciliation job that runs daily for the experiment cohort and flags any tenant deltas >0.5% for manual review.
Jess: Agree. We'll gate wide rollout on zero billing exceptions in 24h.
incidents-bot: Alert suppressed: ingest-p95-burst at 2026-03-21T18:20:27Z (auto-suppressed after deploy)
Mia: OK team, 15m sync tomorrow 10:00 PT to finalize experiment knobs and owners. Please ack if you can make it.
Sam: +1
Ashwin: +1
Jess: +1
Mia: I'll upload experiment measurement sheets and the replay artifact to the RFC thread after the sync.
